_comment: Launch roster for Shmo. ~180 figures across the three categories: Biblical Old Testament, Biblical New Testament, and Syriac patristic/ecclesiastical (bar Salibi's own world), including the adversaries on each side. Every attribute here is a GAME HINT, so an approximate era is a wrong answer, not a rounding error — the Owner must review each entry before the seed script publishes anything. Era is a signed century (-10 = 10th c. BC, 7 = 7th c. AD); there is no century zero. Period is the named epoch beside it — see the period note below. Entries whose dating is conventional, contested, or spans a century boundary carry a _note; the seeder strips every underscore-prefixed key before POSTing. Names follow the full-form convention described below. Relatives and adversaries are dated with the figure they attach to, so a household or a confrontation shares one century. The primeval figures (Genesis 1-11) are marked PRIMEVAL and are the least secure data in the file; adversaries are marked ADVERSARY.
_modellingNotes: PERIOD vs ERA: every figure carries both. Era is a signed century driving Shmo's higher/lower arrow; Period is a named epoch giving an exact-match hint, because higher/lower across -41..14 is a weak signal on its own. Period is NOT derivable from era plus category, which is why it is stored: the 5th century holds both NiceneEra and PostChalcedonian figures, the 10th century BC holds both UnitedMonarchy and DividedMonarchy ones, and Herod the Great is era -1 but period Apostolic. Assignment here is rule-based (see scripts, add-periods) with exactly two overrides — Jeroboam son of Nebat, whose secession splits the 10th c., and Narsai of Nisibis, who outlives Chalcedon by half a century.

Role 'Patriarch' is used for the ecclesiastical office only. The biblical patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob) are 'Other' — Category already separates them, but if you would rather they read as Patriarch, that is a one-line change here, not a schema change.

Pre-Chalcedonian Syriac fathers (Ephrem, Aphrahat, Rabbula, Simeon the Stylite, Bardaisan, Mar Awgin, Febronia, Ibas) are Tradition 'NotApplicable': the West/East Syriac split postdates them, and assigning either would be an anachronism. If you want that to read as its own hint rather than sharing a bucket with pre-Christian figures, add a 'PreChalcedonian' member to HistoricalFigureTradition.
There is no 'Priest' role, so Aaron and Ezra are 'Other'. Worth adding if you want the Aaronic priesthood to be guessable.
The Region enum has no India, so Thomas — the apostle of the East in Syriac tradition — is 'Persia'.

Single primary role forces a pick where figures hold two: John and Matthew are 'Apostle' rather than 'Evangelist' (Mark and Luke, who were not apostles, carry Evangelist); Jacob of Edessa is 'Bishop' rather than 'Translator'.

The primeval figures of Genesis 1-11 (Adam through Nimrod) are dated by CHRONOLOGY, NOT HISTORY, and are the weakest hints in the roster. They follow the Masoretic/Ussher reckoning, which puts creation at c. 4004 BC (era -41). A Septuagint-based chronology puts it near 5500 BC (era -55) and would shift all ten by roughly fourteen centuries. Nothing here is a historical date in the sense the patristic entries are; if that bothers you as game data, drop the ten or give them a shared round era. HistoricalFigure.MinEra was widened from -40 to -60 to admit them, which is a real relaxation of a typo guard: a mistyped year like -1500 is now accepted where it used to be rejected.

Primeval eras are anchored to birth on the Ussher reckoning, so Noah reads as -30 (born c. 2948 BC) rather than -24 (the flood, c. 2348 BC). If you would rather the hint point at the event a player would think of, Noah and Nimrod are the two to revisit.

FULL-NAME CONVENTION: the name is the answer in Shmo, so it must be unambiguous, and case-by-case judgement about which bare name 'conventionally means' whom does not scale. Every figure therefore carries its fullest attested form — a patronymic (Joshua son of Nun, Jeremiah son of Hilkiah), a see or birthplace (Amos of Tekoa, Paul of Tarsus), or an epithet (Elijah the Tishbite, Stephen the Protomartyr). Nothing is invented: a figure with no attested qualifier keeps the bare name, which is why Adam, Delilah, Nebuchadnezzar, Caiaphas, Arius and ten others stand alone — none has a namesake in the roster. The rule is ENFORCED by seed-historical-figures.mjs, which rejects any bare name that shares a given name with another figure, so the convention survives future additions instead of decaying into review comments.

KINSHIP DATING: relatives and associates are dated with the figure they attach to, not independently — Rachel, Leah, Esau and Laban all read -18 with Jacob; the whole Bethany household reads 1. That is honest for a game hint (they are contemporaries) but it means the era hint cannot separate members of one household, and a player who has narrowed to the right century still faces a dozen names. Expect era to be a coarse filter in the biblical categories and a sharp one in the patristic.

Scripture reuses names heavily, so the ambiguity problem will recur on every addition: a second Lamech (Cain's line), a second Zechariah (the minor prophet), a second Simeon (son of Jacob), a second Nathan (David's son) and Matthew's alternate name Levi were all left out of the roster rather than disambiguated. Add them only with a qualifier attached.

The Cainite line (Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, Naamah of Genesis 4) is omitted deliberately. Ussher's chronology dates the Sethite genealogy only, so those four have no anchor at all — not even a chronology-derived one — and any era for them would be invention rather than convention.

ADVERSARIES: the roster models office, not allegiance — there is no alignment attribute, so Herod, Pilate, Jezebel and Arius are indistinguishable from anyone else by their hints, and Judas Iscariot keeps Role 'Apostle' because that is the office he held. That is deliberate: an alignment hint would make many rounds trivially easy. If you ever want it, it is a new enum plus a migration, not a data change.

Herod the Great is era -1 while the rest of the nativity cast is 1: he died in 4 BC. That is correct, not a typo, and it is the only place in the New Testament block where the era hint separates contemporaries.

Nestorius is included as a historical figure. 'Nestorian' as a label for the Church of the East is contested and rejected by that church; nothing in this roster endorses it, and the East Syriac figures (Narsai, Babai, Isaac of Nineveh, Timothy I, Ishodad) carry Tradition 'EastSyriac' on their own terms.

SecondTemple is the one period with no figures in it. It is defined so Maccabean and intertestamental figures have somewhere to go; the gap between Mordecai son of Jair and the nativity is real, not an oversight.

figures.name: Adam
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — dated by chronology, not history. Masoretic/Ussher reckoning (creation c. 4004 BC). A Septuagint-based chronology would put him near -55 instead, and every primeval entry below would shift with him. Region follows Genesis 2:14, which names the Tigris and Euphrates among Eden's rivers.

figures.name: Eve
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — dated with Adam; same chronology caveat.

figures.name: Cain son of Adam
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — first generation after Adam; same chronology caveat.

figures.name: Abel son of Adam
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — first generation after Adam. Read as the first martyr in Syriac tradition, but Role is Other because Martyr in this enum carries the ecclesiastical sense.

figures.name: Seth son of Adam
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3874 BC on the Ussher reckoning.

figures.name: Enosh son of Seth
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3769 BC on the Ussher reckoning. Son of Seth; Genesis 4:26 dates the calling on the name of the Lord to his lifetime.

figures.name: Kenan son of Enosh
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3679 BC on the Ussher reckoning.

figures.name: Mahalalel son of Kenan
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3609 BC on the Ussher reckoning.

figures.name: Jared son of Mahalalel
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3544 BC on the Ussher reckoning. Father of Enoch.

figures.name: Enoch son of Jared
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3382 BC on the Ussher reckoning. Role is Prophet on the strength of Jude 14 ('Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied'); Other is defensible if you would rather reserve Prophet for the writing prophets.

figures.name: Methuselah son of Enoch
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3317 BC on the Ussher reckoning.

figures.name: Lamech son of Methuselah
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 3130 BC on the Ussher reckoning. Son of Methuselah and father of Noah. NOTE: Genesis 4:18 names a second Lamech in the line of Cain; only the Sethite one is in the roster, because two figures cannot share an answer name.

figures.name: Noah son of Lamech
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 2948 BC on the Ussher reckoning; the flood falls c. 2348 BC (-24). Anchored to birth, like the other primeval entries. Region is his Mesopotamian setting, not Ararat.

figures.name: Shem son of Noah
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — born c. 2446 BC on the Ussher reckoning. The Semitic line runs through him to Abraham.

figures.name: Ham son of Noah
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — son of Noah, dated with Shem.

figures.name: Japheth son of Noah
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — son of Noah, dated with Shem.

figures.name: Nimrod son of Cush
figures._note: PRIMEVAL — post-flood; Babel falls c. 2242 BC on the Ussher reckoning. Genesis 10:10 makes Babel the beginning of his kingdom, so King rather than Other.

figures.name: Abraham son of Terah
figures._note: Conventional Middle Bronze dating. Patriarchal chronology is debated and some scholars decline to date him at all.

figures.name: Sarah wife of Abraham
figures._note: Dated with Abraham; same caveat.

figures.name: Lot son of Haran
figures._note: Abraham's nephew; dated with him. Region is Sodom, in the Jordan plain.

figures.name: Hagar the Egyptian
figures._note: Sarah's Egyptian handmaid and Ishmael's mother; Region reflects her origin.

figures.name: Ishmael son of Abraham
figures._note: Genesis 21:21 settles him in the wilderness of Paran; Region is Other because Arabia is not in the enum.

figures.name: Isaac son of Abraham
figures._note: Conventional; one generation after Abraham.

figures.name: Rebecca daughter of Bethuel
figures._note: Born in Paddan-aram (Mesopotamia) but Region follows the Canaan narrative, as for Rachel and Leah.

figures.name: Jacob son of Isaac
figures._note: Conventional; same generation-count basis as Isaac.

figures.name: Esau son of Isaac
figures._note: Ancestor of Edom; Region is IsraelJudah because Edom is not in the enum.

figures.name: Laban the Aramean
figures._note: Stays in Paddan-aram, so Region is Mesopotamia unlike his daughters.

figures.name: Joseph son of Jacob
figures._note: Conventional. Region is Egypt for the vizier narrative, not his Canaanite birth. Renamed from the bare "Joseph" once a namesake joined the roster — the name is the answer in Shmo, so it has to be unambiguous.

figures.name: Judah son of Jacob
figures._note: Son of Jacob and ancestor of the royal line.

figures.name: Levi son of Jacob
figures._note: Son of Jacob and ancestor of the priestly line. NOTE: the evangelist Matthew is also called Levi in Mark 2:14; the roster keeps him under Matthew.

figures.name: Tamar wife of Er
figures._note: Judah's daughter-in-law (Genesis 38); one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy.

figures.name: Moses son of Amram
figures._note: Follows the late-date Exodus (13th c.). An early-date Exodus would put him at -15.

figures.name: Aaron the Priest
figures._note: Priest — no Priest role in the enum. Dated with Moses.

figures.name: Miriam the Prophetess
figures._note: Called a prophetess in Exodus 15:20. Dated with Moses.

figures.name: Jethro the Midianite
figures._note: Priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law. Role is Other because there is no Priest role; Region is Other because Midian is not in the enum.

figures.name: Zipporah daughter of Jethro
figures._note: Moses' Midianite wife; same Region caveat as Jethro.

figures.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Unnamed in scripture, so the descriptive title is the name. Dated with Moses on the late-date Exodus; identifying him with a specific pharaoh is exactly the contested question the roster should not silently settle.

figures.name: Balaam son of Beor
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Numbers 22:5 places him at Pethor by the River. Role is Prophet because that is the office the narrative gives him, whatever it makes of him.

figures.name: Korah son of Izhar
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Leader of the wilderness rebellion, Numbers 16.

figures.name: Caleb son of Jephunneh
figures._note: One of the two faithful spies; dated with the conquest generation.

figures.name: Eleazar son of Aaron
figures._note: Aaron's son and successor as high priest. Role is Other — no Priest role.

figures.name: Phinehas son of Eleazar
figures._note: Aaron's grandson; same Role caveat.

figures.name: Joshua son of Nun
figures._note: Role is Other, not Judge: he precedes the book of Judges and leads as Moses' successor.

figures.name: Delilah
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Judges 16 gives no patronymic, so the name stands bare.

figures.name: Ruth the Moabite
figures._note: Set in the era of the judges; Moabite by birth, but the narrative belongs to Bethlehem.

figures.name: Naomi wife of Elimelech
figures._note: Ruth's mother-in-law.

figures.name: Boaz of Bethlehem
figures._note: Ruth's husband and David's great-grandfather.

figures.name: Samuel son of Elkanah
figures._note: Both last judge and prophet; Prophet chosen as the primary role.

figures.name: Hannah wife of Elkanah
figures._note: Samuel's mother; her song prefigures the Magnificat.

figures.name: Jonathan son of Saul
figures._note: Saul's son and David's friend.

figures.name: Jesse of Bethlehem
figures._note: David's father; the root of Jesse in Isaiah 11:1.

figures.name: Goliath of Gath
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. 1 Samuel 17:4. Region is IsraelJudah because Philistia is not in the enum.

figures.name: Michal daughter of Saul
figures._note: Saul's daughter and David's first wife.

figures.name: Bathsheba daughter of Eliam
figures._note: Solomon's mother.

figures.name: Absalom son of David
figures._note: David's rebel son.

figures.name: Nathan the Prophet
figures._note: The prophet who confronts David. NOTE: David also has a son named Nathan (2 Samuel 5:14), not in the roster.

figures.name: Joab son of Zeruiah
figures._note: David's army commander.

figures.name: Jeroboam son of Nebat
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. First king of the northern kingdom; reigned c. 931-910 BC.

figures.name: Ahab son of Omri
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned c. 874-853 BC; Elijah's royal opponent.

figures.name: Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. 1 Kings 16:31 names her father, king of the Sidonians. Role is Other — queen consort, and King is male-titled in the enum.

figures.name: Athaliah
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned c. 841-835 BC — the one reigning queen of Judah, but Role is Other for the same reason as Jezebel. Worth revisiting if a Queen role is ever added.

figures.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
figures._note: First Isaiah. If the roster ever distinguishes Deutero-Isaiah, that figure would be -6.

figures.name: Sennacherib
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Assyrian king, reigned 705-681 BC; anchored to the start of the reign.

figures.name: Hezekiah son of Ahaz
figures._note: Reigned c. 715-686 BC; Isaiah's royal contemporary. Anchored to the start of the reign, so the 8th c.

figures.name: Jonah son of Amittai
figures._note: Region is Nineveh, where the narrative sits, rather than his native Gath-hepher.

figures.name: Josiah son of Amon
figures._note: Reigned 640-609 BC; the reforming king whose era Jeremiah is called into.

figures.name: Manasseh of Judah
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned c. 697-642 BC. Qualified as "of Judah" to keep him clear of Manasseh son of Joseph, who is not in the roster.

figures.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
figures._note: Spans the boundary: called c. 627 (7th c.), but anchored here to the fall of Jerusalem in 586 (6th c.). -7 is equally defensible.

figures.name: Baruch son of Neriah
figures._note: Jeremiah's scribe. Role is Other — no Scribe role.

figures.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
figures._note: Region is Babylon, where he prophesies in exile.

figures.name: Nebuchadnezzar
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned 605-562 BC, spanning the boundary; anchored to the 6th c., where the fall of Jerusalem and the Daniel narratives sit.

figures.name: Belshazzar
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. The regent of Daniel 5.

figures.name: Daniel the Prophet
figures._note: Narrative setting is the 6th c. exile; critical scholarship dates the book's composition to the 2nd c. BC.

figures.name: Ezra the Scribe
figures._note: Scribe and priest — no Priest or Scribe role in the enum.

figures.name: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah
figures._note: Governor — no Governor role in the enum.

figures.name: Esther the Queen
figures._note: Queen consort; Role King is male-titled in the enum, so Other.

figures.name: Haman the Agagite
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Esther 3:1.

figures.name: Mordecai son of Jair
figures._note: Esther's cousin; dated with her.

figures.name: Mary the Mother of Jesus
figures._note: Renamed from the bare "Mary" once a namesake joined the roster — the name is the answer in Shmo, so it has to be unambiguous.

figures.name: Herod the Great
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned 37-4 BC and died before the era turns, so he is -1 while the rest of the nativity cast is 1. That is correct rather than a typo, and it makes the era hint genuinely discriminating in the New Testament block.

figures.name: Joseph of Nazareth
figures._note: Disambiguated from Joseph son of Jacob, who holds the bare name in the Old Testament.

figures.name: Herod Antipas
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Tetrarch 4 BC - AD 39; anchored to the AD bulk of the reign, unlike his father.

figures.name: Herodias
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Her daughter, traditionally Salome, is left out: the roster already has Salome the Myrrh-bearer and two figures cannot share an answer name.

figures.name: Elizabeth wife of Zechariah
figures._note: John the Baptist's mother and Mary's kinswoman.

figures.name: Zechariah the Priest
figures._note: John the Baptist's father, a priest of the division of Abijah. Role is Other — no Priest role. NOTE: distinct from the minor prophet Zechariah, who is not in the roster.

figures.name: Simeon the Righteous
figures._note: The righteous man of Luke 2 whose canticle is the Nunc Dimittis. NOTE: distinct from Simeon son of Jacob, not in the roster. Renamed from the bare "Simeon": Distinguished from Simeon the Stylite and Simeon of Beth Arsham; the title follows Luke 2:25.

figures.name: Anna the Prophetess
figures._note: Luke 2:36 calls her a prophetess outright, so Prophet rather than Other.

figures.name: Judas Iscariot
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Role stays Apostle — he was one, and the roster records office rather than verdict.

figures.name: James son of Zebedee
figures._note: James son of Zebedee. If you later add James the brother of the Lord, the two names will need disambiguating. Renamed from the bare "James" once a namesake joined the roster — the name is the answer in Shmo, so it has to be unambiguous.

figures.name: James the Brother of the Lord
figures._note: Leader of the Jerusalem church, traditionally its first bishop — hence Bishop rather than Apostle, though Galatians 1:19 calls him one.

figures.name: John son of Zebedee
figures._note: Apostle and evangelist; Apostle chosen as primary. Renamed from the bare "John": John the Baptist already holds the qualified form, so the bare name was genuinely ambiguous between the two.

figures.name: Matthew the Apostle
figures._note: Apostle and evangelist; Apostle chosen as primary.

figures.name: Thomas the Apostle
figures._note: The apostle of the East in Syriac tradition. Region is Persia because India is not in the enum.

figures.name: Paul of Tarsus
figures._note: Region is Asia Minor for Tarsus and the missionary journeys.

figures.name: Mark the Evangelist
figures._note: Region follows the tradition that he founded the see of Alexandria.

figures.name: Luke the Evangelist
figures._note: Region follows the tradition of Antiochene origin.

figures.name: Barnabas the Apostle
figures._note: Cypriot; Region is Asia Minor as the nearest enum value to his mission field.

figures.name: Martha of Bethany
figures._note: Sister of Mary of Bethany and Lazarus.

figures.name: Mary of Bethany
figures._note: Kept distinct from Mary Magdalene and Mary the Mother of Jesus; the three are conflated in some Western traditions but not in the Syriac.

figures.name: Salome the Myrrh-bearer
figures._note: One of the women at the tomb (Mark 16:1).

figures.name: Pontius Pilate
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Prefect of Judaea AD 26-36. Role is Other — no Governor role in the enum.

figures.name: Caiaphas
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. High priest AD 18-36. Role is Other — no Priest role.

figures.name: Annas
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. High priest AD 6-15 and Caiaphas' father-in-law; same Role caveat.

figures.name: Barabbas
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else.

figures.name: Simon Magus
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Acts 8:9-24; the source of the word simony.

figures.name: Timothy of Ephesus
figures._note: Traditionally first bishop of Ephesus. Renamed from the bare "Timothy": Distinguished from the East Syriac catholicos Timothy I, whose regnal name is only one character away.

figures.name: Titus of Crete
figures._note: Traditionally first bishop of Crete; Region is the nearest enum value.

figures.name: Silas the Prophet
figures._note: Acts 15:32 calls him a prophet; Paul's companion on the second journey.

figures.name: Priscilla of Corinth
figures._note: Tentmaker and teacher; with Aquila she instructs Apollos.

figures.name: Aquila of Pontus
figures._note: Priscilla's husband, a Jew of Pontus.

figures.name: Lydia of Thyatira
figures._note: The seller of purple from Thyatira; first named European convert.

figures.name: Bardaisan of Edessa
figures._note: d. 222; born 154, so spans the 2nd-3rd c. Philosopher and hymnographer of Edessa, later judged heterodox. Pre-Chalcedonian, hence NotApplicable.

figures.name: Marcion of Sinope
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Floruit c. 144. One of the three heresiarchs Ephrem writes against by name.

figures.name: Mani
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. c. 216-274, born in Mesopotamia. Ephrem's Prose Refutations answer him directly.

figures.name: Aphrahat the Persian Sage
figures._note: The Persian Sage; Demonstrations written 337-345. Pre-Chalcedonian.

figures.name: Shapur II
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Reigned 309-379; the Great Persecution of Persian Christians falls in his reign, which is why he matters to Syriac history specifically.

figures.name: Julian the Apostate
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Emperor 361-363. Role is King because the enum has no Emperor. Ephrem's Hymns against Julian are contemporary with his death.

figures.name: Arius
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. c. 256-336; the controversy opens 318. Role is Other — he was a presbyter, and the enum has no Priest.

figures.name: Ephrem the Syrian
figures._note: d. 373, Nisibis then Edessa. Pre-Chalcedonian and claimed by both West and East Syriac traditions, so neither can be assigned without anachronism.

figures.name: Mar Awgin
figures._note: Traditional founder of Mesopotamian monasticism; the tradition itself is legendary and the dating is not secure.

figures.name: Febronia of Nisibis
figures._note: Martyr of Nisibis under Diocletian. Included partly to keep the roster from being entirely male after the biblical categories.

figures.name: Rabbula of Edessa
figures._note: d. 435, so just pre-Chalcedon (451).

figures.name: Nestorius
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. Patriarch of Constantinople 428-431, condemned at Ephesus. SENSITIVE: "Nestorian" as a label for the Church of the East is contested and rejected by that church; his presence here is a historical entry, not an endorsement of the label. Tradition is NotApplicable because he predates Chalcedon and none of the three enum values fits him.

figures.name: Eutyches
figures._note: ADVERSARY — the roster has no alignment attribute, so nothing in the data marks this figure as an opponent; Category, era, role and region read exactly as they do for anyone else. c. 380-456, condemned at Chalcedon in 451. Named here because the miaphysite tradition is routinely and wrongly conflated with his position.

figures.name: Ibas of Edessa
figures._note: d. 457. Condemned then restored at Chalcedon; his letter was later anathematised in the Three Chapters. Tradition is genuinely contested here.

figures.name: Simeon the Stylite
figures._note: d. 459. Venerated across the later divisions, so NotApplicable rather than a side.

figures.name: Narsai of Nisibis
figures._note: d. c. 502; anchored to his School of Nisibis career, which begins in the 5th c.

figures.name: Jacob of Serugh
figures._note: d. 521, bishop of Batnan. Born c. 451, so most of his life is 5th c.; anchored to his death and episcopate.

figures.name: Sergius of Reshaina
figures._note: d. 536. Translator of Galen and Pseudo-Dionysius. His own christological allegiance is disputed.

figures.name: Severus of Antioch
figures._note: d. 538. The central theological authority of the West Syriac tradition.

figures.name: Jacob Baradaeus
figures._note: d. 578. His ordinations preserved the miaphysite hierarchy; the name Jacobite derives from him.

figures.name: John of Ephesus
figures._note: d. c. 589. Historian of the miaphysite church.

figures.name: Isaac of Nineveh
figures._note: Briefly bishop of Nineveh but known as the ascetic writer, hence Monk.

figures.name: Marutha of Tikrit
figures._note: d. 649. First maphrian of Tikrit.

figures.name: Athanasius of Balad
figures._note: d. 687. Also a translator of Aristotelian logic.

figures.name: Thomas of Harkel
figures._note: The Harklean New Testament, 616.

figures.name: Paul of Tella
figures._note: The Syro-Hexapla, c. 617.

figures.name: Jacob of Edessa
figures._note: d. 708, so his last years are 8th c. Bishop chosen over Translator/Commentator though he was all three.

figures.name: Timothy I
figures._note: Catholicos 780-823, so the office spans the 8th-9th c.; anchored to its start. -> 9 if you prefer the bulk of the reign.

figures.name: John of Dara
figures._note: Floruit first half of the 9th c.

figures.name: Thomas of Marga
figures._note: Author of the Book of Governors, c. 840.

figures.name: Ishodad of Merv
figures._note: Floruit c. 850.

figures.name: Moshe bar Kepha
figures._note: d. 903, so his last years are 10th c. A principal source for bar Salibi.

figures.name: Elias of Nisibis
figures._note: d. 1046. Chronicler and lexicographer.

figures.name: Dionysius bar Salibi
figures._note: d. 1171, Metropolitan of Amid. The subject of Sabro's own translation work.

figures.name: Michael the Syrian
figures._note: d. 1199. His Chronicle is the major West Syriac history.

figures.name: Bar Hebraeus
figures._note: d. 1286. Maphrian, so Bishop is also defensible; Commentator chosen for the Storehouse of Mysteries.

figures.name: Abdisho bar Brikha
figures._note: d. 1318. Metropolitan of Nisibis; his catalogue of Syriac writers is a key bibliographic source.
